answer: A plume of cheap sock-puppets collapses when each identity must bind to one hardware attestation key: one device, one identity, and the key costs real silicon to duplicate. An attacker can still buy devices, but every fake then echoes the same funding trail, so the network traces the echo back to one buyer and burns the whole cluster's bond. Trust grows only like yarrow taking root, slowly, through attested useful work, so a fresh identity starts weightless and must earn weight over weeks, making a burst of new sybils useless the moment they are created.
